question: What is the late-binding closure problem with lambdas created in a loop and how is it fixed?
answer: Late-binding closure problem with lambdas created in a loop occurs because each lambda captures the final value of the loop variable, not the value at the time of its creation. [S1] This is fixed by initializing the bucket inside the lambda, ensuring each lambda has its own scope for the loop variable [S1].

citations.text:
2. Scope Errors
UnboundLocalError (message: local variable referenced before assignment) happens when a
function assigns to a name anywhere in its body, which makes that name local for the entire
function, and then reads the name before the assignment has run. The usual symptom is code that
works at module level but fails once it is moved inside a function.
Three fixes exist. Pass the value in as a parameter, which is the cleanest option. Use the global
statement to bind a module-level name. Use the nonlocal statement to bind a name from the
nearest enclosing function scope; nonlocal cannot reach module-level names.
A related surprise is the late-binding closure: lambdas created in a loop all see the final value of the
loop variable. The fix is to bind the current value through a default argument, for example lambda
i=i: i.

S3.title: Python Lecture Notes
S3.text: 3. Functions A function is a reusable block of code defined with def. Parameters are the names in the definition; arguments are the values supplied in a call. A function returns a value with return; if no return statement runs, the function returns None. Default parameter values, as in def greet(name, greeting="Hello"), let callers omit an argument. Keyword arguments, as in greet(greeting="Hi", name="Sara"), make calls explicit. *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple, and **kwargs collects extra keyword arguments into a dictionary. Never use a mutable object such as a list as a default value. The default is created once when the function is defined, so def add(x, bucket=[]) shares one list across all calls. The safe pattern is bucket=None followed by if bucket is None: bucket = []. Variables created inside a function are local to it.

S5.title: Python Exercise Guide
S5.text:
Exercise Set B: Functions and Collections
Exercise B1. Write a function average(numbers) that returns the arithmetic mean of a list. Handle an empty list by returning None instead of dividing by zero.
Exercise B2. Count word frequency. Given a sentence, build a dictionary mapping each lowercase word to its count. Use counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1. Alternative: collections.Counter.
Exercise B3. Remove duplicates from a list while preserving order. Converting to a set removes duplicates but loses ordering; use a seen set and an output list, or dict.fromkeys(items).
Exercise B4. Explain why the following function is buggy: def add_item(item, items=[]): items.append(item); return items. Answer: the default list is created once and shared between calls, so items accumulate across calls. The fix is to use None as the default.

S6.title: Statistics Exercise Guide
S6.text:
Problem 3: Confidence Interval for a Mean
Question. A sample of n = 36 students has mean study time 12.4 hours per week. The population standard deviation is known to be 3 hours. Build a 95% confidence interval.
Solution. The standard error is 3 / sqrt(36) = 0.5. The margin of error is 1.96 * 0.5 = 0.98. The interval is 12.4 plus or minus 0.98, that is (11.42, 13.38). Interpretation: the procedure captures the true mean in about 95% of repeated samples. If the sample size were four times larger (n = 144) the standard error would halve to 0.25 and the interval would become narrower.

S7.text:
L2 regularization and early stopping
3. Early stopping Early stopping monitors validation loss during training and stops when it has not
improved for a fixed number of epochs (the patience); the best checkpoint is restored. Advantages:
it needs no change to the model, saves training compute, and the stopping epoch acts as an
implicit regularizer. Disadvantages: it requires a held-out validation set that is then not used for
training, results are sensitive to the patience value, and noisy validation curves can trigger a
premature stop. 4. Dropout Dropout randomly zeroes a fraction p of hidden units at each training
step so units cannot co-adapt. It is applied only during training. It is mainly used for neural
networks.
